angles.cost_others: People around you have stopped asking how business is going, because the answer has a tide in it. Family celebrates your peaks carefully, having attended the troughs. Somewhere in the up-and-down is an average that would support a calm life. Nobody, including you, has ever met it.

angles.drive: Nothing anchors. The city is temporary, the job is a stepping stone, the relationship is seeing where things go, and this has been true for eleven years. Your life is all current and no bed. Movement this constant looks free from the shore. From inside, lately, it just looks like water.
angles.cost_self: The storage unit in your old city still holds boxes from the move before last, paid monthly, visited never. Its contents would furnish the settled life you keep almost starting. The invoice arrives on the third of each month, a small bill for keeping every option open and none taken.
angles.cost_others: Old friends tell stories about you in the past tense while you are still alive and reachable, mostly because your presence never stays anywhere long enough for new chapters. You are missed in four cities, which sounds romantic. The visits stopped being planned around you years ago.

angles.drive: Your energy spreads across so many channels that no single one carries real depth. The five ventures, the three cities, the dozen half-relationships: everything gets a trickle, and trickles evaporate. The delta looks impressive from above. At ground level, none of the streams can float a boat.
angles.cost_self: Tuesday touched four projects in three currencies and finished none of anything. The calls overlapped, the follow-ups queued, and at midnight you were answering messages for the venture that earns the least, because it shouts the loudest. The one that could actually flourish got eleven minutes.
angles.cost_others: Partners in each of your streams believe they have a quarter of you, and the math says less. They compare schedules sometimes, your various people, and find the sum does not close. Everything you touch stays alive and nothing thrives, and everyone waits for a consolidation the current keeps postponing.

angles.drive: You handle resources the way careful water handles a landscape, never taking more than the channel can hold. The purchase gets slept on, the debt gets declined, the plan keeps a margin. Boring, people say, until their own accounts get interesting in the bad way.
angles.cost_self: The car was chosen after the insurance quote, the reliability data, and one conversation with a mechanic you trust. It has now outlasted three of your friends’ flashier choices, at half the total cost. The spreadsheet that picked it is still on your laptop, mildly famous.
angles.cost_others: Friends consult you before their big decisions the way travelers check the depth of a river before driving in. Your questions are unexciting and save fortunes: what does it cost per year, what happens if it breaks. Several disasters in your circle simply never happened. That was you.

angles.drive: Your resources move like a reliable stream, in on schedule, out with intention, never flash-flooding. The salary lands, the transfers fire, the obligations get met a little early. Drama has no purchase on your finances, and the calm compounds as quietly as the interest.
angles.cost_self: Rent has arrived on the first for eleven consecutive years, across three landlords, one recession, and a broken leg. The current landlord once called to check the transfer was real, so rare is the species. You are the tenant reference other applicants wish existed.
angles.cost_others: The people downstream of you, family, dependents, one perpetually struggling friend, plan their lives around a reliability they have stopped noticing. The support just arrives, monthly, like weather in a fortunate climate. Nobody asks what maintaining a stream that steady requires. It requires everything, daily.

angles.drive: The future finds you already provisioned. The renewal date is in the calendar, the emergency fund holds six months, the umbrella lives in the car. Your readiness is so habitual it looks like luck: things simply never seem to catch you without the relevant item.
angles.cost_self: When the layoffs came, your household absorbed the news with a strange calm: the fund was there, the resume was current, the numbers had been run in advance during a peaceful January. The panic that visited every other affected house found yours already interviewed and hired.
angles.cost_others: People tease the preparations right up until they need them, at which point you become briefly, intensely popular. The jump cables, the spare charger, the printed copy: someone borrows one weekly. You have become the reason other people can afford to be spontaneous. Nobody sends a card.

angles.drive: Your resources pool behind walls you keep raising. The money accumulates and does not move, the generosity is rationed through a narrow spillway, and downstream, things that needed watering are visibly dry. The reservoir is impressive. Reservoirs, unvisited, are just deep places holding still.
angles.cost_self: The account crossed the threshold you once named as enough, and the threshold moved the same week, upward, as it always moves. Your niece’s tuition request took three weeks to answer and came back a loan, papered, at interest. Family dinners since have had a different acoustics.
angles.cost_others: People stopped asking, which you registered as peace. The requests dried up, the little fundraisers route around you, and the reputation settled like silt: comfortable, careful, closed. The wealth is real and growing. What it is for remains, to everyone including you, the open question.

angles.drive: Every offer arrives at your door pre-suspected. The deal has a catch, the kindness has an angle, the stranger has a reason: your default read is downstream contamination, and proof of purity is a standard almost nothing meets. You are rarely cheated. You are also rarely surprised by joy.
angles.cost_self: The neighbor’s offer to water your plants during your trip triggered a full risk assessment: motive, key custody, precedent. You declined with thanks and paid a service. The plants did fine. The neighbor waved differently afterward, from slightly further away, permanently.
angles.cost_others: People approach you with their cards face up and their movements slow, having learned that anything else reads as an angle. The honest ones find the screening mildly insulting and mostly stop volunteering. What gets through your filter is genuinely safe. So little gets through.

angles.drive: Letting go, of money, of objects, of the way Sunday is supposed to run, activates something in your grip that logic cannot pry open. The sunk cost stays sunk and held, the worn-out thing stays shelved, and your hands, at any given moment, are completely full.
angles.cost_self: The vacation fund has existed for nine years and never once been spent, each proposed trip failing the final review at the moment of booking. The money is for vacations. The vacations are somehow never quite worth the money. The fund grows, a monument to trips unrisked.
angles.cost_others: Prying anything from you, a concession, an old coat for the charity bag, an admission that plans changed, has a known difficulty rating among your people. They mostly stopped trying and started working around the grip. Your hands hold everything. Notably, lately, that includes very little of theirs.

angles.drive: You get clearer the harder things press, because only pressure stops your guessing. Inside a crisis you want the next move more than the right feeling. If you bring that clear head into a calm week, you keep it for the next crisis.
angles.cost_self: Clear-headed in crisis is the self you trust. Since calm gives you nothing to push on, you chase the next crisis rather than rest in a quiet one. You pay for every skipped quiet week in sleep, and rest counts as much as a crisis.
angles.cost_others: In a crisis you take the clear head and every decision. Deciding fast feels safer than watching anyone decide slowly, so you carry the whole crisis rather than share it. Hand one piece over, because a crisis is learned by holding part of it.

angles.drive: You pick your moment instead of taking the first one offered. Force spent early feels wasted, so a moment picked well beats three taken early. Each time an open door counts as a moment, you stop needing the right time to announce itself.
angles.cost_self: Picking the moment keeps you from wasting yourself. You hold a move until the moment is certain rather than good enough, since an early move cannot be undone. You watch the chance you held back go to someone faster, and the good-enough moment was yours.
angles.cost_others: The moment is yours alone to pick. You would rather keep the plan until the moment than explain it, and you leave the people you lead without a signal. You give up less by naming the moment early than your silence costs the people waiting.

angles.drive: You lead without shouting, often without anyone noticing. You would sooner be right than be obeyed, and you lead by arranging the outcome rather than asking. Whenever you say the plan aloud, your quiet leading reaches past the people already listening.
angles.cost_self: Leading without shouting keeps you out of the argument. Because you would rather lead quietly than be seen asking, you leave your name off most of what you steered. If you claim one of them, leading that leaves a trace starts earning you the rank.
angles.cost_others: Arranging beats asking whenever you lead. Leading without shouting feels cleaner than a request someone can refuse, and you give the people you steer no yes or no. You took their answer by never asking, and leading with one question costs you less than that.

angles.drive: You go cold rather than say what hurt. Going cold keeps you in charge of the hurt, and silence gives no one a way back in. Remember that you stay in the cold as long as anyone you put there.
angles.cost_self: Going cold keeps the upper hand without a word. Since a fight means admitting you were hurt, you would rather go cold than lose the argument. You stay cold long after the fight ends, and it is worth remembering what that costs in closeness.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone crosses you, you go cold on them first. You turn cold rather than show an anger that can be answered, and you take away their only way to fix it. Keep in mind that going cold leaves them a problem with no name.

angles.drive: You are harder on yourself than anyone has been. You would rather catch a fault first than be told, and you are hard on your work before anyone else can be. Bear in mind that being this hard is your choice and yours to lower.
angles.cost_self: Your own work gets the hardest judge you know. Since pleasure in your work feels like dropping your guard, you stay hard on it rather than enjoy it. You pay for being this hard in rest never taken, because nothing you make gets to count.
angles.cost_others: Hard on yourself never stays on yourself. You hold the people close to you to the same hard line rather than a kinder one, since you never let yourself off. You land the hardness on them too, and it was not theirs to carry.

angles.drive: You never let up, on anything or anyone. Since letting up feels like losing, you keep the pressure on rather than call the job done. You cannot feel finished until you let up on the thing you finished, and that is worth keeping in mind.
angles.cost_self: Never letting up is how you prove you belong. Because rest reads as falling behind, you would rather stay under pressure than put it down for a night. You settle the cost of never letting up in sleep, and the body sends the bill.
angles.cost_others: Letting up is something you refuse the people beside you as well. You would rather share the pressure than let up alone, and you keep them at your pace. Never letting up costs them the evenings you gave up, and only you chose it.

angles.drive: You follow through long after the mood that said yes has gone. Following through matters more to you than improving, so you finish the version you announced. You come out ahead by letting a better version in, rather than finishing a worse one you announced.
angles.cost_self: Following through is the part of yourself you count on. Because stopping halfway feels like a broken promise, you follow through on what no longer fits rather than leave it. You give up the chance you wanted most to follow the last plan through.
angles.cost_others: Your follow-through covers everyone attached to the plan. You follow the agreed course through rather than reopen it, and you hold them to a course never rechecked. Ask once midway, since following through on a plan never rechecked costs them the better one.

angles.drive: You earn trust slowly and prefer it that way. You care about being counted on more than being liked, so you earn trust by record rather than by charm. The more warmth you let go first, the sooner slow trust has a place to start.
angles.cost_self: Slowly earned trust is the only trust you believe. You would rather earn trust over a year than be oversold in a day, since quick trust feels false. You hand chances that need you now to someone quicker, and one named strength costs no trust.
angles.cost_others: Trust from you comes as slowly as you earn it. Since easy trust feels false to you, you make a new person earn it rather than let them in. You can end the wait any day, for the warmth was earned before you offered it.

angles.drive: You pace yourself through things other people sprint. Arriving whole counts for more with you than arriving first, and you keep a pace you can hold for years. You have a sprint in you as well, and pacing yourself was never meant to hide it.
angles.cost_self: Your pace is set so that nothing breaks. Since a sprint costs the steadiness you built, you keep your pace rather than take the opening that needs a rush. You lose the openings that needed a rush to the pace that keeps you whole.
angles.cost_others: Pacing yourself paces everyone beside you. You would rather arrive together than let one run ahead, and you keep everyone at your pace. You take a finish of their own from the people you pace to you, and one running ahead takes nothing from you.

angles.drive: You play safe before you know the odds. Keeping what you have feels more like you than reaching, so you take the safe way ahead of the good one. Remember that playing it safe has a price, and you pay it in chances never taken.
angles.cost_self: Playing safe keeps the floor under you. Because a wrong move costs you more than a missed one, you keep playing it safe with the job you have. You let every chance you play safe around close, and the work you wanted goes with it.
angles.cost_others: For everyone waiting on your yes, you play it safe too. You would rather give a safe no than a yes that can fail, and the real answer stays yours. Do not forget that a safe answer leaves them waiting instead of deciding.

angles.drive: You wait for permission that is not coming. Being given permission feels safer than taking it, and you wait to be asked up rather than step up unasked. You hold most of the permission you wait for, a fact you keep forgetting.
angles.cost_self: Waiting for permission keeps you in line. Since permission given feels cleaner than permission taken, you would rather keep your rank than claim the next one. You lose the rank above yours to whoever stopped waiting, and the waiting was your choice.
angles.cost_others: Your waiting for permission gets passed down the line. Since you would rather have permission than have the lead, you hold their answer until yours arrives. Waiting for permission costs them the days you spend waiting too, and you set that clock.

angles.drive: You bite your tongue long before anyone asks you to. You bite down rather than cost the mood, since a smooth evening feels safer to you than an honest one. You keep the peace by biting your tongue, and you alone carry what went unsaid.
angles.cost_self: Safe and unheard is where biting your tongue leaves you. You would rather bite your tongue than put your standing on the line for a point. You hand away the credit for everything you bit back, and a point never made cannot be yours.
angles.cost_others: Your tongue gets bitten hardest around the people who need your answer. You keep things smooth instead of saying what you see, so you bite down while a bad plan passes. Biting your tongue costs them the one no they needed from you.

angles.drive: Going deep is the only way you learn. Half-knowing bothers you more than not knowing at all, so you follow one question down until the floor shows. You pay for the one you own with every subject left at the surface.
angles.cost_self: Where you go deepest is where you are most at home. You would rather stay down with one question than come up for the people and chances passing overhead. You lose nothing of the depth by surfacing a little sooner, and keep the open door.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you go deep, you go alone. Company slows you down, and you pick the quiet ahead of any company you did not choose. Once in a while take someone down with you instead of handing them the summary.

angles.drive: You read what a person is not saying. A pause tells you more than the words around it, so you trust your feeling about someone ahead of the story you are given. Say the reading out loud, because an unsaid one cannot be corrected.
angles.cost_self: Reading a person ahead of their words keeps you from surprises. The reading comes faster than the asking, and you go with it instead of waiting for the rest. Ask the slow question anyway, because the closeness you skip is what being right early costs.
angles.cost_others: Where someone stops short, you read the rest and answer it. Reading them feels like care, and you answer the unsaid rather than wait to be told it. You give the other person back their telling whenever you let the sentence finish.

angles.drive: You teach yourself what matters most to you. A lesson you worked out alone sits deeper than one handed to you, and your own odd route comes ahead of the course on offer. You lose years to the long way and would take it again.
angles.cost_self: Teaching yourself spares you being a beginner anywhere. Working it out alone feels easier than asking someone who knows, and the long road is the one you choose. Ask sooner than you want to, because the help you refuse gets paid for in years.
angles.cost_others: You taught yourself your own route, and it is hard to pass on. Showing the steps means admitting there were none, and you hand over the answer rather than the method. Write the route down, because the way is what anyone learning from you misses.

angles.drive: You think a decision over long after it stopped needing thought. Water comes into you faster than you spend it, and one more angle feels like care rather than delay. You know by now that you only learn from the choices you make.
angles.cost_self: Thinking too much is your way of not being wrong. A wrong call scares you more than a late one, so you think a choice over past its day. Keep in mind that you lose chances this way without a sound, and sleep with them.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone needs an answer, you think it over once more. Getting it right matters more to you than getting it to them, and you hand over the wait. It is worth remembering that you give more by replying now than by replying right.

angles.drive: You keep what you know in until it is finished, and it never is. More goes into you than comes out, because a half-formed thought let loose feels like a thought lost. Remember that you would rather keep an idea safe than see it used.
angles.cost_self: Keeping it in keeps it from being judged. Inside is where an idea stays safe, so you hold yours back until perfect rather than let it out rough. Do not forget that you lose the chance to be heard while waiting to be ready.
angles.cost_others: You keep in what others could use. A thought let out early feels broken to you, so you hold it in rather than hand it over. Remember how much more you help with half an answer than with a whole one never said.

angles.drive: You are hard to reach even from across the table. Most of you lives in an unfinished thought, and you would rather finish it than answer the person in front of you. Remember you are only as reachable as the part that surfaces.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to reach keeps your thinking whole. An interruption costs you the thread, so you answer late or not at all rather than lose it. You already know that you trade closeness for that thread, and closeness does not wait.
angles.cost_others: Hard to reach means a thought is unfinished, and most of yours are. Finishing it comes ahead of the message, and you charge the person waiting in days. Remind yourself that you are worth more fully there than mostly away.

angles.drive: You calm people down without trying to. Taking in someone's worry costs you less than watching them carry it, so you take it in and give back something steadier. Let a little of it out somewhere, because calm you only absorb runs dry.
angles.cost_self: Being the calm one is a job you never put down. You take in other people's upset and level it, while yours waits for a quiet that never comes. You leave your own upset unsettled until you let someone steady you for once.
angles.cost_others: When someone close to you is upset, you become the calm for both. Being needed suits you more than being known, and your own trouble never shows. Let them see you shaken sometimes, because calm with nothing behind it keeps people at a distance.

angles.drive: You soak things up rather than study them. It settles into you from whatever is nearby, so you know a thing long before you can pass a test on it. You can trust the gap, since the proof turns up later than the understanding.
angles.cost_self: Soaking it up is how learning stays with you. Sitting with it until it is yours comes easier than proving it on paper, and the proof is the part you skip. Get the paper once, because the chances asking for it close without you.
angles.cost_others: Soaking up what someone says comes ahead of deciding whether you agree. Taking it in is easier than pushing back, so your disagreement stays where it helps no one. You help more with an honest no than a kind yes, and yours is already there.

angles.drive: Being patient comes easily to you. Letting a thing come in its own time feels more honest than forcing it, and you can wait on a question for months. Keep your pace, because the price is only the chance that needed a push.
angles.cost_self: Being patient also means you never have to ask. Waiting for a thing to come to you feels easier than reaching, so the wanting stays quiet until the chance passes. You gave up what you never asked for without noticing, and one question changes that.
angles.cost_others: You wait for a person to be ready rather than hurry them toward it. Not hurrying feels like respect, and you let someone stay stuck longer than kindness needed. Push sometimes, because being patient is also the hand you kept back.

angles.drive: You let things drift rather than decide them, and you call it patience. There is more Water in you than you turn into motion, so choosing costs more than going along. Remember that when you drift you are choosing too, just not the outcome.
angles.cost_self: Drifting keeps the days quiet, and quiet feels like care. Stirring nothing costs less than reaching, and you renew the lease rather than ask what you want. Do not lose sight of how little you learn of your own wants while nothing changes at home.
angles.cost_others: Whatever you let drift, you leave to someone else. Being carried feels easier than steering, and you let the people close to you make the calls you never did. It helps to remember that you hand them the weight of every call you dodge.

angles.drive: You stay where it is safe long after outgrowing it. Shelter is the thing you trust most, so you pick the known ahead of the better whenever the two come apart. Remember that you keep the shelter even after you walk out of it.
angles.cost_self: Staying in is how you avoid being tested. Not being ready feels more honest than being ready, and you stay long past the day leaving was open to you. Never forget that you give up the very chances the shelter was for by staying in.
angles.cost_others: Staying sheltered keeps you home while others go out. You pick being safe ahead of being there, and watch the invitations thin out instead of going. You hand those you love your safety in place of your company, and the swap is yours to notice.

angles.drive: You over-protect the people you love from what they could survive. Watching someone struggle hurts you more than doing it for them, so the help comes before the asking. Keep in mind how completely you can protect someone, until not even the lesson reaches them.
angles.cost_self: Over-protecting the ones you love never rests. Taking the hit for someone is easier for you than watching them take it, so you carry what was never yours. Bear in mind what you pay in rest for every hit you absorb for another person.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone you love is about to struggle, you over-protect and step in first. Sparing them the hard part feels like love, and you choose their comfort rather than their growing. Remember that you take from them the one lesson that would have stuck.

angles.drive: You start on your own, before anyone has agreed to join you. Needing nobody's go-ahead keeps you free, so you would rather start by yourself than wait for a yes. Let one start wait for company, since starting alone is how you finish alone.
angles.cost_self: Self-starting means you never wait, and never get to be helped. You start alone rather than reach out, since reaching out feels like admitting the start was too big. Ask once before you begin, because the help you skip comes out of your rest.
angles.cost_others: You give a peer your finished start, never your first. Starting without company keeps the idea yours, so you put your own go ahead of anyone's offer to join. Offer someone the rough start sometimes, since you take from them nothing bigger than the beginning.

angles.drive: Side by side is where you are most at ease. Walking side by side matters more than walking out front, so you drop the lead as fast as you refuse to follow. Take the lead sometimes, since the chances out front never come to you.
angles.cost_self: You trust closeness only side by side, so you let a friend near after they match you. You would rather keep your footing than be held up, even when you need it. Be carried sometimes, since the nearness you skip only comes from leaning.
angles.cost_others: You keep every friendship side by side, nobody carried, nobody carrying. Being helped bothers you as much as being led, so you wave off the hand. Let a peer help for a change, since the chance to be needed is one you hold back.

angles.drive: You bounce back faster than most get over the surprise. You would far sooner be upright than seen down, so you stand again ahead of getting over it. Stay down a day longer sometimes, since bouncing this fast never lets the hurt finish.
angles.cost_self: Bouncing back is what you are proudest of and what costs most. You get up rather than stay down to be looked after, because needing help feels like losing twice. Accept the care once, since what you never let in is the price you pay.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you fall, you are back up before anyone can reach you. Standing on your own matters more than being helped up, so you leave people nothing to do. Give a friend one bad day, since being there is what you keep from them.

angles.drive: You go it alone by default, before anyone refuses to help. Waiting on help feels like being slowed, so you do it yourself rather than explain it to anyone. Keep in mind that you are faster alone and not lighter.
angles.cost_self: Going it alone means the whole load sits on one back, yours. You put in extra hours rather than accept the hand, because being helped feels like being less. You pay for every hand not taken out of your own rest, and your body remembers.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a job splits two ways, you carry both ends alone. Holding it yourself matters more than keeping a peer in the loop, so you leave them nothing to carry. Remember that you keep from them half the job and half of you.

angles.drive: Being told is the one thing you cannot take. Your own read feels more solid than any second opinion, so you hold it rather than test it. You stay hard to correct and easy to leave wrong, and the second is the one to remember.
angles.cost_self: Staying uncorrected is a rule you keep at a price. You repeat your own mistake rather than take a peer's version, since yours at least stays yours. You trade being right early for being right alone, remember, and the chance goes with it.
angles.cost_others: You decide a peer's correction is wrong before you hear it. Staying uncorrected matters more than staying in step, so you hand their advice back. Worth remembering, you take from them their one small way of being useful to you.

angles.drive: You wall people out without meaning to, by needing nothing from them. Matching you is rare, so you keep your own company rather than settle. You shut out the right ones as fast as the wrong ones, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_self: Walling people out keeps your standard safe and your evenings empty. You hold out for company that matches instead of company nearby, since near enough feels like settling. You only grow close to whoever sees you at less than your best, and keep forgetting it.
angles.cost_others: You put the wall up highest when someone gets closest. Being seen fine from far matters more than being seen tired up close, so you hold a peer there. Remember that you leave them a friend they can see and never quite reach.

angles.drive: You rise to a dare before deciding if you want it. You wake in a contest like nowhere else, so you weigh the rival ahead of the stakes. Skip a race sometimes, because rising to everything means running some that were never yours.
angles.cost_self: Rising to a dare tells you that you are in the game. You would sooner take a test than take a break, so rest never comes first. Let a win be a rest, because you pay for every race in your own body.
angles.cost_others: You give a friend's dare your full speed before they take it back. Winning in front of a friend matters more than keeping it friendly, so you play every round for keeps. Throw a round once, since what they lose with you is the fun.

angles.drive: Other people's ambition is the kind you catch fastest. You catch a rival's goal faster than you find your own, so you run on borrowed wanting rather than wait. Keep one goal nobody handed you, since half of what you chase began as somebody else's.
angles.cost_self: Catching ambition is quicker than growing it, and you know it. You go after what a rival chases ahead of asking what you want yourself, because wanting alone feels thin. Ask yourself anyway, since the chance nobody else runs for is yours to lose.
angles.cost_others: You catch a friend's plan before they finish the sentence. Running their race feels better than cheering from the side, so you turn their goal into a shared one. Ask if they wanted a partner, because you take a finish meant to be theirs.

angles.drive: On a shared bet, you go all in before anyone asks. Holding back feels like not being there, so you put in your money ahead of reading the terms. Read the terms once, since all in makes you first to pay and last to know.
angles.cost_self: Being all in is how you show you mean it. You put money where your friends are ahead of where your sense is, because holding back feels worse than losing. Keep one stake back a year, since money never kept is the price of company.
angles.cost_others: Beside someone you like, you are all in unasked. You would sooner share the stake than check if they wanted one, so you double a bet that was theirs. Ask first, since you leave them a bet twice the size they chose.

angles.drive: You hate to lose more than you love to win, and the gap shows. You read a rival's win as your loss, since the Fire in you outlasts a single victory. You are keeping a score, remember, that nobody else agreed to play.
angles.cost_self: Hating to lose keeps you in every contest long after it stops paying. You would sooner stay in a losing race than be the first to step off, so you stay. Remember that you give up sleep for every race you refuse to leave.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a friend pulls ahead, you hate it before you are glad. You hear their good news as lost ground, so you answer it with news of your own instead of just listening. Remember that you take a little off every win of theirs.

angles.drive: You spend for show whenever the table is watching. Picking up the bill feels like winning the night, so you pay for everyone rather than let a rival pay for you. You buy the evening, bear in mind, and only rent the goodwill.
angles.cost_self: Spending for show costs more than the bill says. You put the big gesture ahead of the quiet balance, because being seen as generous beats being secure. Worth remembering, you lose money that never returns on a bill with only your name on it.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a friend reaches for the bill, you are already spending for show. Paying matters more than letting them have a turn, so you take their round. You leave them no way to be generous back, and you forget that costs them something.

angles.drive: You are never off, because off feels like falling behind. You would rather run past everyone than stop and ask who was racing you, since you see no finish. You are the one person timing this race, and you forget it most days.
angles.cost_self: Never being off is your pride and what wears you down. You keep the pace up rather than admit you are tired, because tired looks like losing. You repay every skipped rest later and at a higher price, bear that in mind.
angles.cost_others: Even beside a friend you never switch off, handing them a race instead of yourself. Being ahead counts more with you than being beside someone, so you turn a walk into a pace. You deny them, remember, the version of you that is not competing.

angles.drive: Giving is the easiest thing you do. You would rather be useful than be thanked, and you give ahead of being asked. Keep giving this freely, and notice its one price, the flat hour when nothing is needed from you.
angles.cost_self: Something to give away is where you are most at ease. Giving comes before wanting, and you would sooner give one more thing than name what you need. Take a turn too, because your enjoyment is the gift you keep skipping.
angles.cost_others: Whenever the people around you need something, you have given it before they ask. Providing feels safer than receiving, so you hand out more than you let in. Let them give back sometimes, because you have been taking that chance from them.

angles.drive: Enjoying something quietly was never your way. You feel a pleasure fully only once it is shared, and you would rather enjoy a small thing with company than a big thing alone. You pay for enjoying out loud with the private kind, a fair trade.
angles.cost_self: Enjoyment only counts for you when it is shared. You write off an evening alone as wasted, and you pick less enjoyment in company ahead of more by yourself. Learn to enjoy the quiet kind too, because the rest in it is yours to keep.
angles.cost_others: Whatever you enjoy, you pull the people near you into enjoying as well. You run the fun rather than have it, and you leave little for the quieter people to add. Leave some open, because you take the air their smaller pleasures need.

angles.drive: What you make comes out without strain. Ease is the sign you trust, and you do the thing that flows sooner than you force the thing that counts. If it came without effort, you own it a little less, and that is the whole price.
angles.cost_self: Effort was never your measure of worth. You rate what comes easily below what you fought for, so you hand the easy work over free ahead of charging for it. Price the ease too, because the money you wave off is the cost.
angles.cost_others: You make hard things look easy. You show the finished thing sooner than the work, and you leave the people learning from you the ease without the steps. Work at something in front of them once, since you teach more by steps than by ease.

angles.drive: Saying no has never come easily to you. Helping feels more like you than resting does, and you say yes ahead of checking the cost. Remember that every yes comes out of you, and less goes back in.
angles.cost_self: Staying on good terms with whoever asks is what your yes is for. Being needed feels safer than being rested, so you say yes to the evening rather than keep it. Do not forget that you pay for each refused rest with your health.
angles.cost_others: You answer whoever asks first with a yes, and you leave the people at home what is left. Pleasing the person in front of you comes ahead of keeping your word at home. Bear in mind, you owe them the follow-through more than the yes.

angles.drive: You drift toward whatever asks the least of you. You treat comfort as the reward you are owed, and you let a day drift rather than steer it. Worth remembering that you are drifting in a direction too, only not one you picked.
angles.cost_self: Drifting costs you nothing on any single day. Taking it easy feels better than taking it on, so you put off the thing you meant to make again. Look again at the one thing you most wanted to make, because you keep drifting past it.
angles.cost_others: Whatever the people around you decide, you drift along with it. Going along feels better than having a view, and you hand the deciding to whoever is nearest. Try to remember that you leave them carrying choices you were meant to share.

angles.drive: You put pleasure first and the rest after. Feeling good is how you check you are alive, so you take the nicer option ahead of the needed one. Keep hold of this, that you run the pleasure on yourself and it puts nothing back.
angles.cost_self: Pleasure first is the one care you trust. Feeling comforted matters more to you than feeling well, and you take comfort now ahead of health later. You pay for it in the body, and the body keeps a longer memory than you do.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. You take a good time now sooner than a promise kept later, and you spend the house money on the evening. Remember whose share you are spending, since part of it is theirs.

angles.drive: You speak up right where it has gone quiet. You hear silence as agreeing, and you say the unsaid thing rather than sit with it. Keep speaking up, and own its price, since you are remembered for the sentence more than the care behind it.
angles.cost_self: Speaking up is the part of you that never needs rehearsing. You find the clever answer faster than the careful one, and you say it ahead of checking the cost. You close a chance you wanted with a good line more often than you notice.
angles.cost_others: Before anyone asks you to, you speak up for them. Having a voice comes more naturally to you than lending one, so you take the floor ahead of handing it over. Leave the quieter ones the first word, because you speak up on their turn.

angles.drive: You change in front of an audience, for the better. Being watched is where your focus comes from, and you perform a thing sooner than you practice it. You pay for that in private, since nothing you do alone feels quite finished.
angles.cost_self: Performing is how you make things count. Being seen doing it matters more to you than doing it, so you keep performing after the show ends. Give yourself an hour with no one watching, because the rest you skip is the price of the stage.
angles.cost_others: For the people you love, you perform as much as for a crowd. Company feels like a show to you, and your best lines come ahead of your plain self. Save them one plain evening, because you keep performing where you were asked for yourself.

angles.drive: You think fastest with no time to think. You light up under pressure rather than freeze, so you answer on the spot instead of taking it away with you. You rarely give the slow answer its turn, and the speed is worth that most days.
angles.cost_self: Thinking fast is the talent you lean on hardest. You have the first answer before the question is finished, and you trust it ahead of the second. You spend the better answer you never waited for to keep the quickness.
angles.cost_others: Fast enough to finish other people's sentences, you usually do. Waiting for a thought to end feels like wasted time, and you answer ahead of hearing it all. Let the slow thought finish, because you cost the slower ones the rest of theirs.

angles.drive: Talking back comes faster to you than letting it pass. Being told what to do feels like shrinking, and you talk back rather than let a rule stand. Remember that each answer is drawn from you, and you put in less than you spend.
angles.cost_self: Getting pushed around is what talking back saves you from. Being right out loud counts for more with you than being kept on, and you say the thing that ends the conversation. Worth remembering, you talk yourself out of the chances you wanted most.
angles.cost_others: You talk back to whoever asks something of you before the ask is done. You hear a request as a demand, and you answer the tone ahead of the need. Notice how you leave them holding a fight they never brought.

angles.drive: You need an audience more than you need to be right. Being seen is how you know you exist, and you take being watched doing badly over doing well alone. Hold onto this, that you are the one left when the audience goes home.
angles.cost_self: Without an audience, you will not start. Practicing alone feels like wasted effort, and you save the real work for a crowd rather than do it unseen. Never forget that you starve the talent between shows, and between shows is where it grows.
angles.cost_others: What you need from the people close to you is watching more than joining in. You feel company only once it is facing you, and you turn a friend into a crowd. Remember, you take their evening and hand back a show.

angles.drive: You overdo it, and you know it while you do. You never feel enough as a real amount, so you push a thing past its best rather than stop there. Mind that you run out well before the thing does.
angles.cost_self: Overdoing it is how you get a thing noticed. You feel safer with more than with enough, and you give a small occasion the full show. You pay with the body for each full show, and the bill never fails to arrive after the applause.
angles.cost_others: For people who asked for little, you overdo it anyway. You feel a plain yes as too little, so you hand them the full production instead of what they named. Keep track of the extra you leave them to carry beyond what was asked.

angles.drive: You see chances early, at their smallest. Being first matters to you more than being sure, and you move while the chance is only a guess. If you name what you see early, the credit stays yours when it pays.
angles.cost_self: Your eye goes to the far chance before the near one. You look ahead for the next opening more than down at what is in hand. Check what is already yours first, and you stop losing the nearest chance to the far one.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you see a new chance, you bring it to your partners before the last one pays. You would rather share the next idea than finish the current plan. Once you hand them the finished thing, you keep them for the one after.

angles.drive: Giving comes easily to you, often before you have counted. Generosity is how you feel rich, so you would rather give the thing now than keep it for a tighter month. Keep giving as you do, and note what each gift costs you.
angles.cost_self: Giving easily leaves little behind for you. You want the pleasure of giving now more than a cushion later, and now keeps winning. When you set aside the price of one gift each month, you fund the venture you keep giving away.
angles.cost_others: You give in big moments rather than small steady ways. Being generous feels truer to you than being careful, and your family gets the big day and lives through the gap. With small gifts that repeat, you give them the steadiness along with the shine.

angles.drive: In a new venture, you start fast and plan later. The beginning is the warm part, and you would rather open the next one than sit through the middle. When you start fast on fewer ventures, you get to know the ones you start.
angles.cost_self: The easy part for you is the start. You would rather start something new than wait out a long middle, so most ventures end where the rush does. If each fast start must prove itself after the rush, you lose only the weak ventures.
angles.cost_others: You start at full speed, with your partners pulled in beside you. Being at the beginning suits you more than staying for the middle, and the long part lands on them. Name your part before you start, so you ask less of their patience.

angles.drive: The newest thing is what you want. Because new things wake you up, a fresh chance pulls you more than a half-done one holds you. With each chase, you trade away the catch already in your hands, the only one you were sure of.
angles.cost_self: Chasing the new keeps you at the start. Each new chance looks better than the one in hand, so you leave before it pays back. Each time you leave early, you lose the money at the end, and that money is why you chase.
angles.cost_others: Whenever something new shows up, you chase it and leave your partners the middle. You want the next chance more than the ending of this one, since staying put feels like falling behind. Do not forget that every chase costs them the ending you promised.

angles.drive: Spending fast is your reflex. Money is only real to you once it is used, so you spend it now instead of saving it. Bear in mind that fast spending is how you live in the moment, and the moment is all it buys.
angles.cost_self: Fast spending feels like freedom to you. You would rather have the thing now than the money later, and what comes in easily goes before it grows. It is worth knowing that what you spend fast is the stake you never put behind a venture.
angles.cost_others: You spend shared money fast, often before you ask. You put spending on your own call ahead of deciding together, so you hand your family a choice already made. You take their say with each fast spend, and asking first gives it back.

angles.drive: Looking past home comes easily to you. The next venture feels like where your life begins, so you look ahead at what might come rather than at what is here. You are already living the life you look past.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you look past home, you save your best for what comes next. You would rather look toward somewhere new than settle where you already are. You miss the rest your own home was built to give you.
angles.cost_others: You look past the people at home first. Getting to the next venture matters more to you than being with them, so you give them what is left. You lose almost nothing by giving them the first look instead of the last.

angles.drive: Keeping a thing going is the warmest part of you. You would rather keep one thing warm for years than start many, since what lasts feels real to you. Keep it going as you do, and count the dull stretch as part of the work.
angles.cost_self: Keeping something going also keeps you in it past its time. You would rather stay than leave, so you keep putting money into what no longer gives back. When you let go of what has stopped paying, you free your savings for what grows.
angles.cost_others: You keep love going on time and without fail. Reliable feels more like love to you than exciting does, so you give your partner steady warmth ahead of surprise. Give your partner one unplanned evening a month, since you already cover every other day.

angles.drive: Saving comes before spending for you, every time. Something put by is what lets you sleep, so you keep a little back rather than enjoy all of it now. When you save first toward something you want, you get the treat and keep the sleep.
angles.cost_self: Saving first means the fun always comes second. You choose covered rather than comfortable, and the treat you could afford never gets bought. If you give one saved sum a job you enjoy, the saving stops costing you the life it was for.
angles.cost_others: You save first and ask the people at home to wait with you. You put being covered ahead of treating them, since you do the counting. Loosen one line of the budget for them, and your saving starts to feel like care.

angles.drive: Showing up every day is how you love. Being there outranks being exciting for you, and you give the daily thing ahead of the grand one. If you say once in a while that you choose to show up, you keep it from becoming duty.
angles.cost_self: The daily showing up costs you the rest you needed. You put reliable ahead of rested, so you show up on days you have nothing left to bring. Take one day off from showing up, and you bring more to the week after it.
angles.cost_others: You show up daily whether your partner needs it that day or not. Being there makes you feel useful, so you offer presence where a question would serve better. Once you ask what your partner wants that week, you show up with the right thing.

angles.drive: You count everything, the money and the favours and the hours. Counting is your way of feeling safe, so knowing the total comes ahead of enjoying the thing. Keep in mind that the counting protects you from loss and from pleasure in the same move.
angles.cost_self: Counting keeps the fear quiet and the pleasure quieter. You want to know what you have more than to use it, so the money sits counted and unspent. Worth remembering that you give up the use of your savings while busy adding them up.
angles.cost_others: Your count covers the household's spending as much as your own. Knowing where every bit went keeps you calm, and you ask about the receipt ahead of the day itself. Notice that you charge your family a question for every small purchase.

angles.drive: Playing it safe is your first answer. You would rather keep a small sure thing than try for a big maybe, because being safe is what lets you rest. Every time you play it safe, you are also picking which chance to miss.
angles.cost_self: What you already have feels too precious to risk. Reaching for more feels like gambling, and you take the sure thing instead of the bigger one. Over the years, you give up more in missed chances than playing it safe ever saves you.
angles.cost_others: You make the safe call for both of you whenever money is shared. You would rather play it safe than try something new together, so your partner's bigger ideas wait. You lose little safety by saying yes to one small shared plan a year.

angles.drive: Without deciding to, you hold back warmth and money. Giving the whole of yourself feels like spending the last of something, and you give a careful portion rather than the full amount. You hold back more than you need to feel safe.
angles.cost_self: Keeping yourself back spares you hurt and costs you being known. You would rather hold back part of yourself than give the whole, so you stay half known. Remember that the closeness itself is what you lose, since what you keep back cannot be held.
angles.cost_others: You hold back hardest where you love most. You keep a reserve rather than give it all, and your partner gets the careful share only. Never forget that you leave them guessing at warmth you have and keep.

angles.drive: Pressure is where your thinking gets clear. Since you need certainty more than comfort, you let outside pressure clear your head rather than make your own calm. Choose some of that pressure yourself, because you are only this clear with something at stake.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the pressure lifts, your clear head goes with it and a quiet week feels like punishment. You would rather be clear under pressure than at ease without it. Let one quiet week count as rest, because you trade the rest you need for clarity.
angles.cost_others: You bring pressure into calm places. Since you think more clearly under pressure, you put it on the people near you as much as yourself. Keep most of that pressure for yourself, because you take a calm evening from the people at home.

angles.drive: Taking charge comes to you before anyone offers it. Standing by while a group drifts feels worse than being wrong out loud, so you take charge ahead of the vote. Hand the next one over, because you take charge better by choice than by habit.
angles.cost_self: Being in charge weighs on you once you take it. You feel safer in charge alone than sharing it, so you are rarely carried. Let one person carry part of it, because you pay for being in charge by never being looked after.
angles.cost_others: Wherever a plan stalls, you take charge and mean it kindly. Because a slow group feels risky, you take charge rather than wait your turn. Leave the next one to them, since each time you take charge you take their chance to decide.

angles.drive: Nothing at stake feels to you like being passed over. Since you only come awake with something to lose, you take high stakes over sure things. Keep one high-stakes thing going, because you were built to be tested rather than kept safe.
angles.cost_self: Loving high stakes means a calm stretch never feels like a reward. You would rather raise the stakes on a sure thing than let it stay sure. Let something good keep its low stakes, because you spend the calm you could have had.
angles.cost_others: When a day has no stakes, you add some. Since an easy win bores you more than a hard loss, you raise everyone's stakes with yours. Keep high stakes for your own plans, because you take the plain good day from those beside you.

angles.drive: You are harder on yourself than anyone else has been. With Fire past what your strength holds, you would sooner be hard on yourself than let one mistake go. Remember that you never passed a test by going hard on yourself for failing it.
angles.cost_self: Long before anyone sees a mistake, you are already hard on yourself. No day off feels earned under that hardness, so you apologise for rest rather than take it. Bear in mind that being this hard on yourself costs you days off never taken.
angles.cost_others: Your hardness on yourself never stays private. Since you give yourself no pass, you hold those close to you to your standard rather than theirs. Remind yourself that being so hard on yourself in front of them takes the ease from their evening.

angles.drive: Your push arrives before anyone has asked for it. Because waiting for a yes feels like losing ground, you push people along ahead of asking whether they wanted pushing. Do not forget that you push a person as hard as you push a problem.
angles.cost_self: Each time you push too hard, you spend strength you do not have. You would rather push through than keep the energy to finish the week. You pay for pushing too hard in lost sleep, so remember that the bill is yours alone.
angles.cost_others: Pushing people toward an answer is faster than walking them there. Since you trust a push over patience, you push whoever is nearest whether they asked or not. Before the next push, remember that you are harder to be close to than to follow.

angles.drive: Going off duty is an order you never learned to take. Since you feel safe only with something to handle, you stay on duty ahead of ending the day. Remember you were made to meet a crisis rather than stay on duty after it.
angles.cost_self: When one emergency ends, you look for the next rather than go off duty. You never take a rest you did not fight for, so duty is your normal. Only you can call yourself off duty, and waiting costs you every evening at home.
angles.cost_others: Staying on duty is how you love the people in your care. Since being on duty comes easier than company, you give them a guard ahead of someone to sit with. Remember how hard you are to reach when most on duty for them.

angles.drive: Every promise you make becomes a rule you keep. Being relied on is the closest you get to feeling safe, so you keep your word ahead of your freedom to change it. Promise a little less freely, because you keep every one you make.
angles.cost_self: Keeping a promise costs you the right to change your mind. You would rather keep a stale promise than break it, so you stay inside plans past their use. Let yourself out of one, because you turn down better offers to keep old promises.
angles.cost_others: To you, a passing promise is one to keep. Because a promise is a rule rather than a wish, you hold everyone to every one they make. Let small promises go, since you leave your friends no freedom to have only been talking.

angles.drive: By the book is the only way you trust a thing done. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book ahead of the shortcut. Stay with the book, because you are the standard the work gets checked against.
angles.cost_self: Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book decide what you knew. Allow the book one exception, because you give up chances that cannot wait.
angles.cost_others: Doing it by the book counts as respect paid forward. Because you want it right more than fast, you hold a friend's rushed job to the book too. Name the book out loud first, since you take the easy way from everyone beside you.

angles.drive: A fairly earned title is worth more to you than any praise. Since an earned rank says you belong, you earn the next title ahead of chasing the next thrill. Let the title come slowly, because you are already doing the job it names.
angles.cost_self: Earning the title comes first, claiming it long after. You want to look deserving more than to be paid, so you earn it twice before asking once. Claim it now, because earning it this slowly leaves money you were owed on the table.
angles.cost_others: Where titles are concerned, you make everyone earn theirs too. Since an unearned rank looks like cheating, you give a colleague the long route rather than a quiet word. Say the word sometimes, because you take from them the years that earning costs.

angles.drive: A rule you learned once stays in force after it stops helping. The rules that steady you also hold you in, until you keep the correct one ahead of the useful one. You wrote most of these rules yourself, and you can retire them.
angles.cost_self: Between a rule and a chance, you take the rule. You put being correct ahead of being free, so your career keeps the rules and never jumps. Bear in mind that you keep each rule at the price of jobs you never went for.
angles.cost_others: Keeping to the rules is how you look after people. Because one exception feels like a collapse starting, you give them the rule ahead of what they asked for. Never forget that you hand the rules holding you in to everyone living with you.

angles.drive: Fear of slipping runs under most of what you do well. Since your standing holds your worth, you would rather never be seen to slip than be at ease. Remember how much less you are watched for a slip than watching for one.
angles.cost_self: One slip stays with you longer than with anyone who saw it. Afraid to slip, you put looking steady ahead of feeling rested, until good days tire you like bad ones. Remind yourself how much rest you lose over slips you never made.
angles.cost_others: Hiding every slip is how you serve those who depend on you. Since a visible slip reads as failed duty, you offer them a composed self ahead of a true one. Before hiding the next slip, remember that you take their chance to help.

angles.drive: Every duty offered gets a yes before you check its cost. Since being counted on is where your standing lives, you never say no to the next request ahead of finishing the last. Remember you can only say yes for as long as you last.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you say yes, you spend hours promised to yourself. Because holding things together comes ahead of getting home, you trade sleep for another duty. You are nobody's standard once you run out of sleep to say yes with, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_others: Saying yes to everyone keeps your place in their lives. Because a refusal feels like lost standing, you give everyone a slice rather than anyone your whole self. You will want to remember that you give those who need you most whatever is left.

angles.drive: You see finished things where others see empty air. The business before the market exists, the picture before the first stroke, the version of a person they have not met yet. The visions arrive lit from inside, complete, and your job is mostly transcription.
angles.cost_self: You described the neighborhood’s future to a skeptical friend in 2019, cafe by cafe, almost address by address. You were renting there anyway when the wave arrived. The friend brings up that walk every time property prices come up, in the tone people use for eclipses.
angles.cost_others: People dismiss your predictions at intake and quote them at parties three years later. The pattern has repeated enough that a few colleagues now write down your stray remarks, timestamped, as a hobby. Their notebook, they say, outperforms their financial advisor. They are not entirely joking.

angles.drive: Your mind switches on when the world switches off. After eleven, the connections arrive: the insight, the fix, the strange idea with the workable center. Daylight-you executes what midnight-you discovers, a two-shift operation everyone mistakes for one ordinary person.
angles.cost_self: The solution to the storage problem arrived at 1:40am, complete, while the house slept, and you built the prototype by breakfast using a lamp and a towel to muffle the drill. The team spent Tuesday marveling. You spent Tuesday napping, having already been to Wednesday.
angles.cost_others: People learn to check their messages in the morning for your timestamps: 12:51, 2:14, 3:03, each carrying something the daylight meetings could not produce. Employers have stopped policing your hours. Whatever happens in your small hours arrives at standup already glowing, and nobody audits a lighthouse.

angles.drive: Your knowing arrives without visible sources. The diagnosis before the tests, the reading of a stranger at a glance, the sense that this flight, this deal, this person is wrong. Asked to explain, you produce nothing auditable. Asked to be right, you mostly are.
angles.cost_self: You told your friend not to take the apartment, unable to name a single concrete reason beyond the light felt wrong. She took it. The mold survey, the neighbor situation, and the landlord’s lawsuit all surfaced within the year, in roughly the order your discomfort had.
angles.cost_others: People consult you off the record, slightly embarrassed, the way executives consult weather folklore before big launches. Your hit rate embarrasses them further. Nobody builds a slide around your feelings, and increasingly nobody signs anything big without, casually, asking what your gut says first.

angles.drive: One idea takes the whole house. The new interest arrives like ignition: gear bought, sleep skipped, meals forgotten, conversation rerouted through the topic for weeks. The heat is genuine and total, and everything else in your life stands in its light, waiting, unwatered.
angles.cost_self: The chess phase lasted seven weeks and consumed roughly two hundred hours, four apps, one physical clock, and every anecdote you told. Then, on an unremarkable Thursday, it simply stopped burning. The board is under the bed now, with the telescope, the loom, and the kanji cards.
angles.cost_others: Your people track your obsessions like weather systems: naming them, estimating duration, planning around the blast radius. They have learned not to invest in the current one and not to mention the last one. What they miss, quietly, is the version of you between fires. He rarely visits.

angles.drive: Your energy arrives on a schedule no one, including you, can publish. Tuesday-you rewires the kitchen at midnight and Thursday-you cannot answer a text. Plans made in a bright phase get inherited by a dim one, and both phases sign your name with equal authority.
angles.cost_self: You committed to the weekend workshop during Monday’s blaze, prepaid and enthusiastic, and arrived at Saturday as a different person, one who sat in the parking lot for forty minutes and drove home. The refund window had closed. The pattern, your partner noted, has a subscription.
angles.cost_others: People quote two versions of you and specify which one they mean: bright-you and gone-you. Invitations come with soft confirmations layered in, checked twice, once at acceptance and once the night before. Nobody calls it unreliability to your face. The scheduling apparatus around you says it hourly.

angles.drive: Your inner world drifted from the shared one by degrees. The interests nobody around you shares, the hours nobody keeps, the references that land on silence: each pulled you a little further offshore. People love you from the mainland. The commute between you has gotten long.
angles.cost_self: At the reunion you spent the evening at the edge of three conversations, fluent in none of them, holding your drink like a permission slip. The people were kind and the kindness had distance in it. You left early, relieved, and the relief troubled you the whole drive home.
angles.cost_others: Old friends describe you now with the phrase in their own world, said warmly and with a small shrug. Invitations still come, at holidays, in the plural, addressed to a version of you they remember. The estrangement was nobody’s decision. It accumulated, like heat leaving a house.

angles.drive: Your presence is the warm center other lives arrange themselves around. People come in from their cold weeks and hold their hands out to you, mostly without noticing the gesture. The warmth is steady, unconditional, and quietly expensive to maintain. Nobody sees the fuel line. You are the fuel line.
angles.cost_self: Sunday afternoons at yours have become load-bearing for at least five people, including one who mostly sits near the conversation without joining it. Nothing is organized. Soup happens, light happens, and everyone leaves warmer than they arrived. The tradition has no name and perfect attendance.
angles.cost_others: People describe your home with their shoulders, dropping them. New partners get brought to you early, unofficially, for climate testing. The warmth you offer asks no questions, and it has become the family’s reference temperature. Holidays anywhere else get compared to it, quietly, in the car home.

angles.drive: You warm other people’s small flames on principle. The shaky first attempt, the half-announced dream, the try that failed: each gets your specific heat, aimed at the part that was brave. People attempt things in your presence they would not risk elsewhere. That is the whole climate you run.
angles.cost_self: Your niece showed you eleven seconds of a song she was too shy to finish, and your response, proportionate and warm and precise, is why there is now an EP. She thanked you in the liner notes for hearing it before it existed. You framed nothing. You remembered everything.
angles.cost_others: People rehearse their announcements on you first, using your reaction as the prototype for braver telling. The pattern is invisible until you map it: half the leaps in your circle checked their footing against your encouragement first. You are the base camp several summits never mention.

angles.drive: Time near you repairs people. The burned-out friend, the post-hospital parent, the teenager mid-storm: they sit in your warmth doing apparently nothing, and leave with something reattached. You never announce a treatment. You just keep the light on and the questions gentle, and mending happens.
angles.cost_self: Your brother spent three weekends on your couch after the divorce, barely speaking, watching cooking shows. You fed him, asked nothing, and let the couch work. On the fourth weekend he fixed your cabinet hinge, unprompted, whistling. You both understood the hinge was a discharge summary.
angles.cost_others: There is a folding of people into your care that everyone recognizes and nobody has named: after the bad news, so-and-so should probably go to yours. It is spoken like protocol. Your spare bed has hosted more recoveries than some clinics, at a fraction of the paperwork.

angles.drive: Your warmth removes obstacles that were doing important work. The struggle gets pre-solved, the consequence intercepted, the difficulty warmed away before it could teach anything. The people you love stay comfortable and stay soft, and the softness eventually presents its own bill, addressed to them.
angles.cost_self: Your son’s overdue essay got rescued by your midnight edit, again, the fourth rescue this term. His grades are excellent and weightless. The teacher suspects, the boy knows, and some part of him has begun to calculate, correctly, that finishing things is optional in a heated house.
angles.cost_others: Other adults watch you absorb consequences meant for people you love, and bite their tongues at various speeds. The kids are lovely and unweathered. Where resilience should be forming, there is instead a well-tended warmth, and everyone except you can see the forecast it cannot survive.

angles.drive: Being needed became your fuel, and the tank runs low without it. The empty nest, the recovered friend, the crisis that resolves: each healthy ending registers somewhere in you as a small layoff. You keep people slightly cold, unconsciously, to stay employed as their warmth.
angles.cost_self: When your daughter said the therapy was working and she felt genuinely okay, your joy arrived with a strange undertow you inspected later, alone. That week you called her twice with concerns she did not have. She noticed. The okay-ness held anyway, which helped and hurt.
angles.cost_others: People manage their independence around your feelings, staging their strength gently, keeping small needs alive for you like pilot lights. It is tender and slightly backwards, everyone caring for the caregiver by performing need. The healthiest thing anyone could give you is nothing to fix. Nobody dares yet.

angles.drive: Comfort has lowered your flame to standby. The naps lengthen, the plans soften, the day organizes itself around warmth and ease, and ambition visits like a former colleague, fondly and briefly. Nothing hurts. Nothing much happens either, and the two facts are holding hands.
angles.cost_self: The afternoon disappeared again into the warm chair, the blanket, the something on in the background. The course tab is still open from Tuesday, bookmarked under a nap. At six you surfaced, cozy and faintly disappointed, and made tea, which resolved the disappointment into evening.
angles.cost_others: Your people have stopped scheduling you before noon or after eight, fitting themselves into your waking window with practiced ease. Plans involving you acquire cushions automatically. The affection is intact, and the shared unspoken knowledge too: the fire is banked so low now, it mostly keeps itself warm.
